module.2_2: Notes on the E and A strings

l111.title: Meet your bass
l111.objective: Name 9 parts of the bass and identify the 4 strings by name and by sound.
l111.s1: “The bass ties the drums' rhythm to the chords. Without bass, the band floats.”
l111.s2: Headstock and tuning pegs, neck, frets and markers, body, pickups, bridge, volume and tone knobs, and the cable jack.
l111.s3: From thickest to thinnest: E, A, D and G. The thickest is on top, closest to your face.
l111.s4: “The thickest string sounds the lowest. Low is on top, high is at the bottom.”
l111.c1b: Tuning pegs, a neck with frets, a body with pickups and bridge, the knobs and the cable jack.
l111.c2b: 4th E, 3rd A, 2nd D and 1st G. They're numbered from thinnest to thickest.
l111.c3b: The thicker the string, the lower its sound. That's why open E is the lowest note on the bass.
l111.ear: Listen. Which open string is it?
l111.play: Play the open string that lights up.

l114.title: Tuning to E-A-D-G
l114.objective: Tune all 4 strings with the tuner and check them by ear.
l114.s1: “Strings drift out of tune with weather and use. That's why you tune before every practice.”
l114.s2: The tuner has a needle and a circle that turns green when the note is right on.
l114.s3: “If the note goes up, you're on track. If you overshoot, go down a bit and come back up.”
l114.s4: Trick: fret 5 on one string sounds the same as the next open string.
l114.c1b: Green: in tune (±5 cents). Left: too low, tune up. Right: too high, tune down.
l114.c2b: Turn it a little at a time. The direction depends on the bass: watch whether the needle goes up or down.
l114.c3b: Fret 5 on E = open A. Fret 5 on A = D. Fret 5 on D = G.
l114.ear: Listen to both sounds. Is the second one higher or lower?
l114.tune: Tune each string until the circle turns green.

l121.title: Alternate plucking
l121.objective: Pluck alternating index and middle fingers (i-m) with a steady pulse at 60 bpm.
l121.s1: “Your fingers walk just like your feet: one, then the other.”
l121.s2: Your thumb rests on the pickup. The finger pulls the string toward the body and comes to rest on the next string.
l121.s3: Two mistakes: always using the same finger, and pulling the string outward.
l121.s4: “One note per click. i, m, i, m.”
l121.c1b: Index (i) in blue, middle (m) in orange. The thumb rests on the pickup.
l121.c2b: Repeating one finger tires you out. Pulling the string outward makes it snap.
l121.walk: Finger walk: alternate i and m with the metronome.
l121.playE: Open E string in quarter notes, alternating i and m.
l121.playEA: One bar on E and one on A, alternating.

l131.title: One finger per fret
l131.objective: Fret with fingers 1 to 4 on frets 1 to 4 and play “the spider” on one string.
l131.s1: Your thumb sits behind the neck, level with your middle finger. Fingers curved, as if holding a ball.
l131.s2: “Press with your fingertip, nice and curved, like a little hammer.”
l131.s3: Finger 1 on fret 1, finger 2 on fret 2, and so on up to 4: one finger per fret.
l131.s4: “If your hand hurts, stop and shake it out. Playing shouldn't hurt.”
l131.c1b: Fingers are numbered 1 (index) to 4 (pinky). The thumb has no number.
l131.c3b: On the E string, frets 1 to 4 are F, F♯, G and G♯.
l131.fb: Tap frets 1, 2, 3 and 4 on the E string, in order.
l131.hint: Count the frets from the nut.
l131.spiderE: The spider on the E string: 1-2-3-4 in quarter notes.

l132.title: The sweet spot
l132.objective: Press right behind the fret so the note rings clean, with as little pressure as possible.
l132.s1: “Hear that buzz? That's my finger, far from the fret.”
l132.s2: Press right behind the fret. There the string rests on the metal and the note rings clear.
l132.s3: “Squeeze like you're juicing a lemon and you'll get tired. A light touch is enough.”
l132.s4: Close to the fret, curved finger, light pressure: a clean note.
l132.c1b: Right behind the fret, on the nut side. Not on top of the fret and not in the middle of the space.
l132.c2b: Start light and press a little harder until the buzz goes away. That's all the pressure you need.
l132.c3b: Move your finger closer to the fret and press with the fingertip, finger curved. Check that no other finger touches the string.
l132.q1: Where does the note ring cleanest?
l132.q1o2: In the middle of the space
l132.q1h: Think of scene 2 of the cartoon.
l132.q2: The note buzzes. What do you try first?
l132.q2o2: Press as hard as I can
l132.fb: Tap frets 1, 2, 3 and 4 on the A string, in order.
l132.play: On the A string, each fret twice: 1-1-2-2-3-3-4-4. Make every note ring clean.

l133.title: The spider walks back
l133.objective: Play the spider going down (4-3-2-1) with your fingers already in place.
l133.s1: “The spider walks backwards too. Without tripping!”
l133.s2: Rest all four fingers on frets 1 to 4. Play and lift 4, then 3, then 2, then 1.
l133.s3: “Lift your whole hand at once and the spider falls. One finger at a time.”
l133.s4: Going down, the next finger is already in place: you just lift the one in front.
l133.c1b: To go down from 4 to 1, start with all four fingers in place. For each note, lift one finger and play.
l133.c2b: While your fingers walk, your thumb stays put behind the neck.
l133.fb: Tap the spider going down: frets 4, 3, 2 and 1 on the E string.
l133.q: You go from fret 4 down to 3. What does your fretting hand do?
l133.down: The spider going down on the E string: 4-3-2-1 in quarter notes.
l133.updown: Up and down on the E string: 1-2-3-4-4-3-2-1.

l134.title: Changing strings
l134.objective: Move the spider from one string to the next without breaking the beat.
l134.s1: “I made it to fret 4… now what? On to the next string!”
l134.s2: After finger 4 on the E string, finger 1 goes to fret 1 on the A string, right on time.
l134.s3: “Stop to look for the fret and the band keeps going without you.”
l134.s4: Get the next finger ready while the note rings: that way the beat never breaks.
l134.c1b: From fret 4 on one string to fret 1 on the next: finger 1 travels while 4 is still ringing.
l134.c2b: The finger that plucks moves to the new string and you keep alternating i and m.
l134.q: You played fret 4 on the E string. Where does finger 1 go?
l134.qo1: To fret 1 on the A string
l134.qo2: To fret 5 on the E string
l134.qo3: To fret 1 on the G string
l134.qh: The spider climbs string by string: E, A, D and G.
l134.fb: Tap the spider on the E string and keep going on the A string: 1-2-3-4, 1-2-3-4.
l134.EA: The spider on E and A, twice, without breaking the beat.
l134.DG: The spider on D and G, twice, without breaking the beat.

l135.title: The full spider
l135.objective: Play the spider across all 4 strings, up and down, at 70 bpm.
l135.s1: “Today the spider walks across all four strings. Will you join me?”
l135.s2: Climb from E to G with 1-2-3-4. Come down from G to E with 4-3-2-1.
l135.s3: “If you make a mistake, don't start over: keep the beat going.”
l135.s4: The spider is your everyday warm-up: two minutes before you play.
l135.c1b: Up: 1-2-3-4 on E, A, D and G. Down: 4-3-2-1 on G, D, A and E.
l135.c2b: A mistake doesn't stop the music. Keep the beat and fix it on the next note.
l135.ear: Listen: first open E, then a note on frets 1 to 4. Which one is it?
l135.fb: Tap the spider going down: frets 4, 3, 2 and 1 on the G string, then on the D string.
l135.full: The full spider: climb across all 4 strings and come back down.

l141.title: Reading tab
l141.objective: Read from the tab which string and fret to play.
l141.s1: “This isn't scary sheet music: it's your 4 strings, drawn.”
l141.s2: In tab, the bottom line is the E string, the thickest one. The top line is the G string.
l141.s3: “Does 3 mean finger 3? No: it means fret 3. And 0 is the open string!”
l141.s4: Line = string. Number = fret. Read it from left to right.
l141.c1b: Each line is a string. From bottom to top: E, A, D and G.
l141.c2b: The number tells you which fret to press. 0 means open string.
l141.c3b: Read it from left to right, like text. The vertical lines separate the bars.
l141.q1: In tab, which string is the bottom line?
l141.q1h: It's upside down from how you see your bass while playing.
l141.q2: You see a 2 on the second line from the bottom. What do you play?
l141.tab: Read the tab and tap each note on the fretboard.
l141.play: Now on your bass: the same tab in quarter notes.

l142.title: The beat
l142.objective: Keep a steady beat with the metronome and hold it when the click goes quiet.
l142.s1: “Feel that thing that makes your foot tap? That's the beat.”
l142.s2: The metronome marks the beat with a click. We count beats in groups of 4: 1, 2, 3, 4.
l142.s3: “If the click goes quiet, don't rush: the beat keeps going.”
l142.s4: Bass and drums look after the beat for the whole band.
l142.c1b: It's the steady heartbeat of the music. You mark it with your foot or your head.
l142.c2b: We group beats in fours and count 1, 2, 3, 4. On the metronome, 1 sounds louder.
l142.q: How many beats do you count in each bar in these lessons?
l142.click: Tap the beat with the metronome for 4 bars.
l142.alone: Now the click stops halfway. Keep tapping the beat.
l142.play: Four quarter notes on each open string: E, A, D and G.

l143.title: Whole, half and quarter notes
l143.objective: Recognize whole, half and quarter notes and play them for their full length.
l143.s1: “Some notes go by fast, and others stay a while.”
l143.s2: A quarter note lasts 1 beat, a half note 2 and a whole note 4: it fills the whole bar.
l143.s3: “A half note isn't a quarter note in a hurry: let it ring for two beats.”
l143.s4: Quarter 1, half 2, whole 4. Count while it rings.
l143.c1b: Filled head and a stem. It lasts 1 beat.
l143.c2b: Hollow head with a stem. It lasts 2 beats.
l143.c3b: Hollow head, no stem. It lasts 4 beats: a whole bar.
l143.q1: How many beats does a half note last?
l143.q2: Which note fills a 4-beat bar on its own?
l143.tab: Tap each note and listen to how long it lasts for its note value.
l143.play: A whole note, two half notes, four quarter notes and another whole note. Let each one ring.

l144.title: Counting out loud
l144.objective: Count 1, 2, 3, 4 out loud while you play mixed note values.
l144.s1: “I count out loud. That's not for beginners: that's what pros do.”
l144.s2: Say “1, 2, 3, 4” with the metronome. Every note starts on one of those numbers.
l144.s3: “If you get lost, wait for the next 1 and come back in.”
l144.s4: Counting out loud tells you where every note sits in the bar.
l144.c1b: A half note on 1 rings through 1 and 2; the next note starts on 3.
l144.c2b: If you get lost, don't stop: wait for 1 of the next bar and carry on.
l144.q: A bar has a half note, a quarter note and a quarter note. On which number does the second quarter note start?
l144.qh: The half note takes up 1 and 2.
l144.tempo: Count out loud and tap the beat. The click stops after 2 bars.
l144.tab: Read the tab while counting every beat out loud.
l144.play: Play the line counting out loud: half notes, quarter notes and a whole note at the end.

l145.title: Steady beat
l145.objective: Hold the beat for 24 beats without a metronome and play a 4-bar line read from tab.
l145.s1: “Today the metronome takes a break. Can you keep the beat?”
l145.s2: First 8 beats with the click, then 24 without it. Count in your head.
l145.s3: “If you rush, no big deal: breathe and get back on the beat.”
l145.s4: With a steady beat and tab, you're ready to read your first bass lines.
l145.c1b: Count in your head and tap your foot. The metronome is a help, not a crutch.
l145.c2b: While you play one bar, look at the next one.
l145.pulse: 8 beats with the click and 24 without. Keep the beat.
l145.tab: Read the 4-bar line on the fretboard.
l145.play: Play the line on your bass, counting all 4 bars.
